outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Overview: Why Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning
outline.description: Introduce the challenge of adapting large foundation models efficiently and motivate orthogonal approaches to preserve pretrained knowledge. Provide a high-level view of Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT) and how Butterfly OFT (BOFT) improves parameter efficiency while keeping expressivity and stability.
subtopics: The rise of foundation models and the cost of full finetuning
Three PEFT paradigms: model finetuning, adapters, prompt/prefix tuning
Core idea of OFT: preserving neuron pairwise angles
Why parameter efficiency matters: memory, speed, and deployment constraints
Limits of block-diagonal OFT and the need for dense-yet-structured orthogonal updates
BOFT in one sentence: factorize dense orthogonal transforms into sparse butterfly components
High-level contributions of BOFT
Roadmap of the textbook

outline.chapter_title: Prerequisites: Linear Algebra, Optimization, and Spectral Basics
outline.description: Review essential math and ML background to understand orthogonal finetuning and butterfly factorization. Emphasize properties of orthogonal matrices and why spectral behavior affects training stability.
subtopics: Vectors, matrices, norms, and singular value decomposition
Orthogonal and unitary matrices: definitions and properties
Spectral norm, Lipschitz constant, and training stability
Skew-symmetric matrices and the Cayley transform
Block matrices, permutations, and sparsity patterns
Optimization basics relevant to PEFT (initialization, regularization, stability)

outline.description: Survey parameter-efficient finetuning methods, highlighting strengths and trade-offs. Establish where orthogonal finetuning fits relative to low-rank and adapter-based methods.
subtopics: Full finetuning vs PEFT: compute, memory, and generalization trade-offs
Adapter tuning: architectural inserts and inference latency
Prompt/prefix tuning: task-conditioning via inputs
LoRA and low-rank reparameterization
Dynamic rank allocation variants (adaptive LoRA, DyLoRA, etc.)
Reparameterization strategies beyond low-rank
Where OFT/BOFT sit in the PEFT design space

outline.description: Explain OFT’s core mechanism: applying a learned orthogonal transformation shared across neurons in a layer to preserve relational information. Analyze its parameterization, benefits, and limitations.
subtopics: Motivation: preserving pairwise angles among neurons
Multiplicative update: R W0 versus additive updates
Cayley parameterization to enforce orthogonality
Block-diagonal OFT: definition, parameter counts, and training recipe
Advantages of OFT: stability and generalization
Limitations: parameter counts for dense orthogonal matrices and rigid sparsity
Why rigid block patterns may hurt expressivity

outline.chapter_title: An Information Transmission View of Orthogonal Matrix Factorization
outline.description: Introduce a unifying graphical perspective to design sparse factorizations that yield dense orthogonal matrices. Use this lens to derive desiderata for parameter-efficient designs.
subtopics: From matrices to communication graphs: nodes, edges, and layers
Interpreting nonzeros as allowable information flow
Factorization as multi-stage transmission across levels
Desiderata: dense connectivity and minimum free edges
Orthogonality constraints and edge dependencies
Why block-diagonal fails to ensure dense connectivity
Design space for sparse-to-dense factorizations via transmission graphs

outline.chapter_title: Butterfly Structures: From FFT to Efficient Information Flow
outline.description: Build intuition for butterfly graphs as efficient communication topologies. Connect Cooley–Tukey FFT decomposition to sparse factors that collectively realize dense transforms.
subtopics: Recap: Cooley–Tukey FFT and radix-2 decomposition
Butterfly graphs as efficient broadcast/exchange networks
Matrix view: butterfly factors and components
O(d log d) edges and why that matters for parameter efficiency
Comparison to naive dense connectivity and block-diagonal structures
Relevance to ML: fast transforms and structured priors

outline.description: Formalize butterfly matrices, their recursive construction, and their parameterization. Prepare the ground for orthogonal butterfly components used in BOFT.
subtopics: Defining butterfly factors and components
Recursive construction for dimension d = 2^N
Block-butterfly generalization with block size b
Permutations and equivalence classes of butterfly components
Parameter counts and sparsity patterns across stages
Practical handling of non-power-of-two dimensions (padding and grouping)

outline.description: Present the BOFT method that composes a dense orthogonal matrix from a product of sparse orthogonal butterfly components. Detail the algorithm, parameterization, and complexity.
subtopics: Design goals: dense orthogonal update with O(d log d) parameters
BOFT parameterization R(m, b) as a product of orthogonal butterfly components
Cayley-based construction for each 2b x 2b block
Identity initialization for multiplicative updates
Multiplicative Dropout: definition, rationale, and procedure
Parameter counts: dependence on d, m, and b
Computational complexity: training-time overhead and inference folding
Recovering OFT as special cases (m = 1, b = d)

outline.description: Analyze expressivity, spectral behavior, and implicit biases of BOFT. Provide intuition for why the method generalizes well while remaining parameter-efficient.
subtopics: Expressivity comparison: BOFT vs block-diagonal OFT (same b)
Approximation of random dense orthogonal matrices
Kaleidoscope hierarchies and full orthogonal group coverage via products
Spectral norm preservation and implications for stability
BOFT as learning a bilinear similarity under orthogonality
Inductive bias from butterfly structure and structured sparsity
Trade-off between expressivity and regularity

outline.description: Provide practical guidance for integrating BOFT into layers of LLMs, ViTs, and diffusion models. Cover shapes, placements, and engineering tips for stable, efficient training.
subtopics: Where to apply BOFT: attention projections, output projections, and MLPs

outline.description: Summarize empirical results of BOFT on vision, language, and text-to-image diffusion tasks. Discuss metrics, baselines, and the qualitative behavior observed.
